Fourth Street Market Hall No Longer Tallest Proposal in Marin County

Fourth Street Market Hall pedestrian view, rendering by Urbal Architecture

By: Andrew Nelson 5:30 am on October 19, 2026

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:58
Instaread

The formal development application has been submitted for an eight-story senior living facility at 924 Third Street in downtown San Rafael, Marin County. The Fourth Street Market Hall and Residences proposal has been significantly reduced in scale since the preliminary application filed earlier this year, shifting from a skyline-defining 24-story tower to a midrise complex. Goldstone Management is responsible for the application.

Fourth Street Market Hall corner view, rendering by Urbal Architecture

Fourth Street Market Hall corner view at A Street and 4th Street, rendering by Urbal Architecture

The roughly 85-foot-tall structure is expected to total about 326,550 square feet, including 191,600 square feet of housing, 24,950 square feet of commercial retail, and 33,400 square feet for ground-level parking. Parking will be provided for 261 cars via stackers, along with 173 bicycle spaces. Residential amenities will include a theater, library, lobby, activity room, courtyard deck, indoor pool, and a top-floor sky lounge.

The project will include 197 senior independent living rental units, including nine units set aside for low-income households. The developer will also contribute $3.5 million toward the city’s Affordable Housing Fund. Apartment sizes will vary, with 108 one-bedrooms and 89 two-bedrooms.

Fourth Street Market Hall facing 3rd Street, rendering by Urbal Architecture

Fourth Street Market Hall vertical cross-section, illustration by Urbal Architecture

Kirkland-based SRM Development is now listed as the project developer and contractor for the proposal. SRM Development has brought in two Seattle-based firms, with Urbal Architecture to oversee the design, and Fazio Associates to oversee landscape architecture. The exterior will be clad with brick veneer, stucco, wood-like material, concrete, and fiber cement.

Preliminary plans for 924 3rd Street called for a 24-story mixed-use tower with 345 apartments above a similarly-sized market hall.

Fourth Street Market Hall civic space diagram, illustration by Urbal Architecture

924 3rd Street site plan, illustration by Studio KDA

The 1.4-acre property will be located between 3rd Street, 4th Street, A Street, and Lootens Place. Future residents would be in the center of San Rafael, surrounded by restaurants and shops, and just a few blocks away from a grocery store.

Rhoades Planning Group is working as the project’s planning consultant. The estimated cost and timeline for construction have not yet been shared.

Affordable Housing Proposed at 88 Vivian Street, San Rafael

88 Vivian Street Building 2, illustration by Arris Studio Architects

5:30 am on September 12, 2026 By Andrew Nelson

Preliminary plans have been filed for an affordable housing complex at 88 Vivian Street by the canal waterfront in Southeast San Rafael, Marin County. The project plans to replace a bowling alley and surface parking with two apartment buildings with more than a hundred units. AMG Land Development is responsible for the development.

88 Vivian Street Building 1, illustration by Arris Studio Architects

The master plan will produce two structures yielding around 123,640 square feet, including 124 apartments, 179 vehicle spaces, and 170 bicycle spaces. Building 1 will rise three floors, and Building 2 will rise four floors. Apartment sizes will vary with 12 studios, 57 one-bedrooms, and 55 two-bedrooms. The ground level of both structures will be predominantly dedicated to private parking, with some amenities on the ground floor of Building 1.

The project will be fully affordable with two manager units, 98 low-income units, and 24 moderate-income units. The application seeks to invoke the State Density Bonus Law, Senate Bill 330, and the Housing Accountability Act to streamline the approval process and increase residential capacity above base zoning.

88 Vivian Street site plan, illustration by Thomas Phelps Landscape Architecture

San Luis Obispo-based Arris Studio Architects is responsible for the design, with Thomas H. Phelps overseeing the landscape architecture. Illustrations show a podium-style apartment complex with some repetitive facade articulation and varied materials to visually reduce the overall massing.

The 2.4-acre property sits at the corner of Belvedere Street and Vivian Street, on a block bounded by Francisco Boulevard and Louise Street. The site is a block away from San Rafael Creek in a neighborhood dominated by low-slung apartment buildings, commercial structures, and small warehouses.

88 Vivian Street outlined approximately by YIMBY, image via Google Satellite

The estimated cost and timeline for construction have not yet been shared.
